title: Sharp analysis of sketched least squares and randomized low-rank approximation
summary: Two widely used randomized algorithms are the sketch-and-solve method for least-squares regression and the randomized SVD for low-rank approximation. These algorithms apply a random embedding to compress a target matrix, and they perform computations on the compressed matrix to save computational cost. This paper asks, what is the optimal random embedding in these algorithms? Also, what is the sharpest possible error bound for the optimal embedding?
